headline: Oil climbs on a Houthi refinery claim, while the Dow shakes off a 1,000-point drop
paragraphs: Oil rose on Wednesday after Yemen's Houthis said they had struck Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery. Saudi officials said air defences shot down four drones over the site and did not say the refinery was hit. Even so, the claim was enough to put some risk premium back into prices. US crude (WTI) settled about 2.4% higher near US$84 a barrel, and Brent traded above US$93 during the session. Short covering before the holiday and uncertainty ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting added to the move.

Wall Street had a wild session. Hotter-than-expected inflation data, with core PCE at 3.3%, came alongside new 20% tariff plans and another chip sell-off. Together they sent the Dow down more than 1,000 points early on. It recovered to close 0.3% higher at 50,183. The S&P 500 slipped 0.25% and the Nasdaq fell 0.6%, as Nvidia dropped almost 4%. US markets are closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving.
